subject: Business Models
title: Identity Verification
description: A short lesson to help you apply Identity Verification.

hook.text: Would you get in a stranger's car? Uber shows you the driver's name, photo, rating, and license plate.

buildup.text: Identity verification transforms anonymous strangers into accountable participants.

discovery.text: Airbnb requires government ID, phone verification, and social media linking. Each layer adds trust.

twist.text: Tighter verification reduces fraud but also reduces signups. Every friction point loses potential users.

climax.text: Marketplaces must balance security against ease of access. Too strict or too loose, both kill growth.

punchline.text: Name, photo, rating, license plate. Trust is built in layers.

quiz.question: What is the trade-off of strict identity verification?

details.summary: Identity verification in marketplaces confirms that participants are who they claim to be through government ID checks, background checks, social profile linking, and biometric verification. Stronger verification builds trust but adds friction that can reduce sign-ups and participation rates.
details.whyItMatters: Verification is the foundation of marketplace safety. Airbnb requires ID verification. Uber screens drivers. Professional marketplaces verify credentials..
takeaways: Verification methods include government ID, background checks, and biometric scans
Stronger verification builds trust but creates friction that reduces sign-up completion
Verification rigor should match the risk level and intimacy of the transaction type

faq.question: What verification levels are appropriate for different marketplace types?
faq.answer: E-commerce marketplaces may need only email and payment verification. Home-sharing requires government ID and sometimes background checks. Childcare and healthcare marketplaces need credential verification and thorough background screening. Financial marketplaces require full KYC compliance.

faq.question: How do marketplaces balance verification rigor with user experience?
faq.answer: Progressive verification adds requirements as users engage more deeply. Light verification for browsing and messaging, full verification before transacting. Social profile linking provides soft verification without formal processes. Delayed verification after initial sign-up reduces drop-off rates.
